body.statement:
Fix \(d=1\), \(E=3\), and an integer \(r\) with \(3\leq r\leq R_{\max}\).  There exist compatible interior bounds and centered independent compound-Poisson source families for which, with
\[
 a=(1,2)^\top,
 \qquad b=(2,-1)^\top,
\]
the latent cumulant-shift profile is a positive multiple of \(a\), while the treatment-noise profile is a positive multiple of \(a\) plus a binomial finite-difference perturbation in direction \(b\) that vanishes below order \(r\) and equals a nonzero multiple of \(r!b\) at order \(r\).  Both source laws change in every pair of environments.  For each environment pair the scalar calibration contrast is nonzero and the legal source swap gives an observationally equivalent, unequal-effect, no-breakout representation.  Jointly, the original parameter has \(r^\star=r\) and is identified, whereas the swapped latent profile leaves the maintained one-dimensional plane at order \(r\), so the pairwise swap is not a legal joint alternative.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(r\in\{3,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\), and write
\[
 a_0=b_0=0,
 \qquad (a_1,a_2)=(1,2),
 \qquad (b_1,b_2)=(2,-1).
\]
For \(1\leq j\leq r\), put
\[
 \nu_{rj}=(-1)^{r-j}\binom rj,
 \qquad
 \Delta_{r,k}=\sum_{j=1}^r\nu_{rj}j^k.
\]
The binomial identity
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^r(-1)^{r-j}\binom rj e^{jt}=(e^t-1)^r
 \tag{12}
\]
and differentiation at \(t=0\) give
\[
 \Delta_{r,k}=0\quad(1\leq k<r),
 \qquad
 \Delta_{r,r}=r!.
 \tag{13}
\]

Choose \(\eta,\zeta,\varepsilon,L_u,L_t>0\) with
\[
 L_t>2\varepsilon\max_{1\leq j\leq r}|\nu_{rj}|.
 \tag{14}
\]
For each \(e\in\{0,1,2\}\), let \(N^u_e\) be Poisson with intensity
\(L_u+\eta a_e\), and set
\[
 \epsilon_{u,e}=N^u_e-(L_u+\eta a_e).
\]
For the treatment source, take independent Poisson variables \(N^t_{e,j}\) with intensities
\[
 \lambda^t_{e,j}=L_t+\zeta a_e\mathbf 1\{j=1\}
                    +\varepsilon b_e\nu_{rj},
 \qquad 1\leq j\leq r,
 \tag{15}
\]
and set
\[
 \epsilon_{t,e}=\sum_{j=1}^rj(N^t_{e,j}-\lambda^t_{e,j}).
\]
Inequality (14), together with \(|b_e|\leq2\), makes every intensity in (15) strictly positive.  Take an independent centered Gaussian \(\epsilon_y\), and make all sources mutually independent within each environment.  Centering is explicit.  Because the jumps are bounded and the Poisson intensities are finite, each source has finite absolute moments of every integer order; in fact its moment generating function is finite for every real argument.

For a centered compound-Poisson sum with jump sizes \(j\) and intensities \(\lambda_j\), direct differentiation of
\[
 \log\mathbb E\exp\!\left{t\sum_jj(N_j-\lambda_j)\right}
 =\sum_j\lambda_j(e^{jt}-1-jt)
 \tag{16}
\]
shows that its cumulant of every order \(k\geq2\) is \(\sum_j\lambda_jj^k\).  Hence the two environmental source profiles, relative to environment \(0\), are
\[
 u_k=\eta a,
 \qquad
 w_k:=
 \bigl(\kappa_k(\epsilon_{t,e})-
       \kappa_k(\epsilon_{t,0})\bigr)_{e=1}^2
 =\zeta a+\varepsilon\Delta_{r,k}b.
 \tag{17}
\]
Both source families change in every environment pair: the coordinates \(a_0,a_1,a_2\) are pairwise distinct, and, by (13), the treatment-source second-cumulant difference between environments \(e\) and \(f\) is \(\zeta(a_e-a_f)\neq0\).

Set
\[
 \alpha=1,
 \qquad \beta=-q/2,
 \qquad \gamma=q,
 \tag{18}
\]
where \(q>0\).  By source independence and cumulant additivity, (17) gives
\[
 c_k=u_k+w_k
     =(\eta+\zeta)a+\varepsilon\Delta_{r,k}b.
 \tag{19}
\]
Since \(r\geq3\), equations (13) and (19) imply
\[
 C=[c_2]=[(\eta+\zeta)a],
 \qquad
 A=\operatorname{span}\{a\}.
 \tag{20}
\]
The calibration vector is nonzero.  Moreover,
\(a^\top b=1\cdot2+2\cdot(-1)=0\), so (13), (19), and the orthogonal-projector definition yield
\[
 Q_Ac_k=0\quad(3\leq k<r),
 \qquad
 Q_Ac_r=\varepsilon r!b\neq0.
 \tag{21}
\]
Thus the original joint parameter has \(r^\star=r\).  Its latent profiles \(u_k=\eta a\) lie in \(A\) at every order, so the population identification theorem applies and identifies the structural effect \(-q/2\) from the joint laws.

Now choose the fixed coefficient bounds so that
\[
 a_0+\rho<1<a_1-\rho,
 \qquad
 q_0+\rho<q<q_1-\rho,
 \qquad
 q/2<B-\rho.
 \tag{22}
\]
Choose \(\kappa_0>0\) with
\[
 \kappa_0+\rho<(\eta+\zeta)
 \min_{e\neq f}|a_e-a_f|=\eta+\zeta,
 \tag{23}
\]
and choose \(M\) above the maximum \((2R_{\max}+\delta)\)-moment of the finitely many source variables in the construction and their swapped versions, with margin \(\rho\).  Such an \(M\) is finite by (16).  These choices make the original and swapped coefficients and sources interior whenever they are restricted to any two environments.

Indeed, for a pair \(e\neq f\), the one-dimensional observed calibration contrast is
\[
 c_2^{ef}=(\eta+\zeta)(a_e-a_f)\neq0.
 \tag{24}
\]
It has magnitude at least \(\eta+\zeta>\kappa_0+\rho\), so it has rank one and its column space is all of \(\mathbb R\).  Consequently its orthogonal projector is zero and every order is pairwise no-breakout, for both source labelings.  The source-swap algebra gives, within that pair,
\[
 T'_e=T_e,
 \qquad Y'_e=Y_e,
 \qquad
 \beta'=-q/2+q=q/2.
 \tag{25}
\]
Equations (22)--(24) and the choice of \(M\) make both pairwise representations legal members of the corresponding swap-safe interior.  Their effects differ by \(q>0\).

Joint legality fails for the swapped representation for a precise reason.  Under the swap its latent source is the original treatment source, whose order-\(r\) profile is, by (13) and (17),
\[
 w_r=\zeta a+\varepsilon r!b.
\]
Because \(b\neq0\) and \(b\perp a\), this vector does not belong to \(A=\operatorname{span}\{a\}\).  The swapped joint parameter therefore violates the latent-profile-plane condition and is not in \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\), although every one-dimensional pairwise restriction satisfies that condition automatically.  This proves simultaneous pairwise ambiguity and joint three-environment rescue.
body.justification: The construction is the explicit joint-rescue certificate: all three environment pairs retain a legal unequal-effect source ambiguity, but the joint orthogonal direction identifies the effect.
body.gap: It establishes only the demonstrated intersection with the two-environment obstruction, and does not claim that the new low-rank class contains every simultaneous-shift model considered by Kivva et al.
body.consumer: It explains why three suitably heterogeneous protein-signaling environments can carry identifying geometry that is absent from every pairwise reduction.
